coast-fire: Estimate the savings you need today to coast toward retirement.
fire: Explore your financial independence target and a path toward it.
lean-fire: Explore a retirement plan built around a lean spending budget.
fat-fire: Model a retirement target around your higher-spending lifestyle.
barista-fire: Explore how part-time income could reduce your portfolio needs.
rmd: Estimate a required minimum distribution using your account assumptions.
hsa: Explore contributions, withdrawals and potential HSA account growth.
brrrr: Estimate cash left in a deal, refinance proceeds and rental cash flow.
rent-vs-buy: Compare renting and buying over a fixed 30-year projection.
mortgage-vs-invest: Compare extra mortgage payments with investing under your assumptions.
mortgage-payoff: Explore how extra payments could change payoff time and interest.
house-affordability: Estimate a home budget using income, debts and housing costs.
pmi: Estimate private mortgage insurance costs under your assumptions.
heloc: Explore payments across a home equity line of credit’s phases.
debt-snowball: Explore a payoff plan that targets smaller balances first.
debt-avalanche: Explore a payoff plan that targets higher interest rates first.
credit-cards-payoff: Plan payments across multiple cards with one monthly budget.
roas: Calculate return on ad spend and explore break-even targets.
landed-cost: Estimate the total and per-unit cost of getting goods to destination.
break-even: Estimate the sales needed to cover your fixed and variable costs.
roi: Calculate total or annualized return from investment cost, returned value and holding period.
cap-rate: Calculate an unlevered property cap rate from annual NOI or a rental worksheet, with assumed target-rate values.
credit-card-minimum-payment: Estimate a user-defined card minimum, changing repayment cost and the effect of paying extra.
drip: Compare reinvesting after-tax dividends with keeping dividends as cash under the same external contributions.
roth-conversion-ladder: Track separate five-tax-year conversion dates, outside-cash tax costs and an early-retirement funding bridge.
cash-on-cash-return: Calculate a simple cash yield or a first-year rental cash return after financing and a capital reserve.
house-hacking: Estimate monthly owner-occupied housing costs after tenant rent and the separate initial cash needed to buy.
rental-property: Project annual rental cash flow, loan balances and sale proceeds using explicit holding-period assumptions.
noi: Build property net operating income from rent, vacancy and itemized operating expenses before financing.
seller-financing: Model an owner-financed note, monthly payments and the balloon due at maturity.
fix-and-flip: Estimate house flipping profit, pre-sale cash funding and the break-even sale price.
stock-profit: Estimate stock profit or loss after fixed or percentage trade fees and cash dividends.
stock-average: Add stock purchases to calculate quantity-weighted cost, shares and invested cash.
discount-points: Compare two fixed-rate mortgage quotes, upfront points and costs at a sale or refinance horizon.
covered-call: Compare a standard covered-call buy-write with shares alone at expiry, including fees and capped upside.
compound-interest: Project compound growth with contributions, or compare nominal interest rates and effective annual yield.
investment: Solve for an investment’s ending value, monthly contribution, return, starting amount or time under stated assumptions.
margin: Calculate selling revenue, cost, profit margin or markup; additional modes cover stock and currency margin.
markup: Calculate selling price from cost and markup, or compare markup with gross profit margin.
mortgage: Estimate principal, interest and entered housing costs, with editable payment and extra-payment assumptions.
amortization: Build a loan repayment schedule and separate principal from interest using your payment assumptions.
rent: Estimate an affordable monthly rent budget from income and an editable affordability limit.
debt-to-income-ratio: Compare entered monthly debt payments with gross monthly income; this is not a lender approval.
refinance: Compare refinancing costs and payment assumptions with the existing loan at your chosen horizon.
apr: Estimate a borrowing APR using the entered loan costs and payment assumptions, not a lender disclosure.
fha-loan: Estimate FHA payments and modeled mortgage insurance using entered loan and housing-cost assumptions.
va-mortgage: Estimate VA loan payments and modeled funding fees using entered eligibility and loan assumptions.
home-equity-loan: Estimate a home equity loan payment from the borrowed amount, term and assumed interest rate.
down-payment: Estimate a down payment, purchase price or cash requirement under your selected calculation mode.
biweekly-mortgage: Compare a biweekly mortgage repayment assumption with a regular monthly payment schedule.
mortgage-recast: Compare mortgage recasting with an unchanged loan or principal prepayment using entered fees and rates.
mirr: Calculate a modified internal rate of return from cash flows, a finance rate and a reinvestment rate.
interest: Project interest and account growth using your contribution, compounding and other selected assumptions.
finance: Solve a time-value-of-money variable using consistent cash-flow signs, periods and payment timing.
interest-rate: Solve the loan rate implied by a balance, term and fixed monthly payment, excluding borrowing fees.
savings: Project savings growth or estimate the contribution or time needed to reach a goal under stated assumptions.
simple-interest: Solve simple interest, principal, time or rate using interest that does not compound.
cd: Estimate certificate-of-deposit growth using entered rates and compounding; this is not a bank quote.
bond: Estimate bond price, yield or other fixed-coupon terms, with a separate settlement-date pricing mode.
mutual-fund: Project mutual-fund account growth and fee effects from editable contributions and return assumptions.
average-return: Compare arithmetic and compound returns or analyze entered cash-flow and variable-period return data.
irr: Estimate internal rates of return for entered periodic or dated cash flows; review root and timing limitations.
payback-period: Estimate when modeled cash flows recover an initial investment, with selected discounting assumptions.
present-value: Discount a future lump sum or annuity to a present value using entered rate and timing assumptions.
future-value: Project a future value from a starting amount and payments using the selected compounding assumptions.
inflation: Compare historical purchasing power or model a hypothetical inflation path; projections are not forecasts.
cagr: Calculate compound annual growth from endpoints or dates, without treating external cash flows as returns.
investment-fee: Estimate the long-term effect of investment fees or compare two fee assumptions under the same growth model.
real-return: Convert nominal and inflation-adjusted returns using consistent rate and purchasing-power assumptions.
tax-equivalent-yield: Compare tax-equivalent yields using entered federal and state tax assumptions; no personal tax advice.
treasury-bill: Estimate Treasury bill price, proceeds or yield conventions from entered terms, not live auction quotes.
business-loan: Estimate business-loan payments, interest and entered borrowing costs under the selected repayment assumptions.
depreciation: Compare book depreciation methods and schedules; this is not an automatic tax depreciation determination.
quick-ratio: Calculate a quick ratio from liquid current assets and current liabilities, with explicit inclusion assumptions.
current-ratio: Compare current assets with current liabilities using totals or an itemized working-capital worksheet.
discount: Calculate sale price, savings, reverse discounts or two stacked reductions; taxes and promotion rules are separate.
sales-tax: Add sales tax or recover a pre-tax amount from an entered rate; the tool does not determine local taxability.
commission: Estimate a sales commission using entered rates and calculation bases rather than inferring an employment contract.
self-employment-tax: Estimate 2025 or 2026 regular self-employment tax and the SE portion of Additional Medicare tax; excludes ordinary income and state taxes.
salary: Convert gross salary across pay frequencies and work schedules before tax, payroll deductions and benefits.
auto-loan: Estimate a vehicle payment or price using entered loan, trade-in, rebate, tax and fee assumptions; this is not a dealer quote.
personal-loan: Compare loan installments, origination fees and net proceeds under the selected fee treatment, without assuming lender approval.
credit-card: Estimate a single card payoff using fixed payments, a deadline or an editable minimum-payment rule; actual statements may differ.
debt-consolidation: Compare existing debt payments with a proposed consolidation loan, including entered origination fees and financing choices.
retirement: Explore retirement saving targets, contributions, withdrawals and longevity under constant return and inflation assumptions.
401k: Explore 401(k) savings, employer matching and withdrawal scenarios; projection modes reuse 2026 limits rather than forecasting future rules.
emergency-fund: Choose reserve months to estimate a cash target, savings gap or deposit schedule without assuming a universal reserve recommendation.
budget: Normalize income, spending and savings allocations to monthly amounts using an entered flat tax percentage, not a paycheck tax calculation.
